main_text.p: ma, quod derepente uires resoluat, aut ipsa febris non admodum, uel acuta, uel pernici-osa sit.
main_text.head: EXERC. XXVIII.
BVBONVM ET CARBVNCVLORUM pestilentium curatio.
main_text.p: Tametsi bubonum & carbunculorum pestilentiū cura physico aliena uidea-tur, quòd manus actioné & ferramen-ta postulet, non tamen absq; physici ratio-ne æger sanitati restitui potest. Idcirco utrunque genus tumoris præter naturam, q; malignas & summas pestilentes febres comitatur, curam aggredi, nos exercendi gratia, non erubescemus. Quod in primis bubones sint adenum inflammationes, dubitant perpauci medici Hippocratis, Galeni & Æginetæ, atq; cæterorum ueterum doctrina, scientiaq; edocti. Propterea uiscus aliquod, uel inflammatum esse, uel aliqua maligna lue affectum necessariò significat.

In præcipuis enim nobilium partium emis-sarijs, nimirum sub auribus, aut sub alis, aut in inguinibus oriri semper consueuerunt. Qui igitur in pestilenti febre oriuntur, non solùm inflammatum esse, uel cerebrū, uel cor,

page.notes: The drop capital T of "Tametsi" is large and joined to the word. The word "actioné" has a tilde over the e, which I read with some confidence. The first line is a fragment continuing from the previous page, so it is marked cont="true". The printed line "ma,quod derepente" is set with the comma closed up to the preceding word in the printer's style, which I have kept as "ma, quod". The catchword "cor," is the last word of the page, printed alone at the right below the text.
